translations.title: Add and Subtract Within 10
translations.explanation: Add and Subtract Within 10 is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Adding, Subtracting, and Working with Data”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.OA.B.2. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies.2 By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers. Instructional focus: Students connect quantities, counting strategies, equations, and story situations so that addition and subtraction represent meaningful relationships rather than isolated facts. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Add and Subtract Within 10. Addition combines or increases quantities; subtraction separates, compares, or finds an unknown part. Equal sign means both expressions have the same value. Counting on/back, making ten, decomposing numbers, and inverse-operation reasoning are valid strategies when they fit the quantities.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: Start with 8 counters and add 3 more. The total is 8 + 3 = 11. A related subtraction fact is 11 - 3 = 8. Example 2: Start with 9 counters and add 5 more. The total is 9 + 5 = 14. A related subtraction fact is 14 - 5 = 9.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: represent 8 objects. Step 2: join 3 additional objects. Step 3: count or decompose the combined quantity to obtain 11. Step 4: check the relationship by subtracting 3 from 11; the result is 8. Step 1: represent 9 objects. Step 2: join 5 additional objects. Step 3: count or decompose the combined quantity to obtain 14. Step 4: check the relationship by subtracting 5 from 14; the result is 9.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Add and Subtract Within 10. Do not treat the equal sign as an instruction to write the next answer. Do not change a story relationship merely to make the arithmetic easier. Check whether the chosen operation and the final number are reasonable for the situation.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Add and Subtract Within 10. Represent the quantities, choose an addition or subtraction relationship, calculate with a suitable strategy, and check the result against the original situation.

Główny kierunek pracy: Uczeń łączy liczebność zbiorów, strategie liczenia, równania i sytuacje tekstowe, tak aby dodawanie i odejmowanie opisywały rzeczywiste zależności, a nie tylko pojedyncze fakty rachunkowe. Tytuł i kolejność pochodzą z zaakceptowanego źródła pedagogicznego, natomiast granice merytoryczne wyznaczają oficjalne standardy Common Core.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Cel tej lekcji: Dodawanie i odejmowanie — Add and Subtract Within 10. Dodawanie łączy lub zwiększa ilości; odejmowanie rozdziela, porównuje albo wyznacza brakującą część. Znak równości oznacza tę samą wartość po obu stronach. Liczenie w przód i wstecz, dopełnianie do dziesięciu, rozkład liczb oraz działania odwrotne są poprawnymi strategiami.
translations.workedExamples: Przykład 1: Mamy 8 liczników i dokładamy 3. Razem jest 8 + 3 = 11. Powiązany fakt odejmowania to 11 - 3 = 8. Przykład 2: Mamy 9 liczników i dokładamy 5. Razem jest 9 + 5 = 14. Powiązany fakt odejmowania to 14 - 5 = 9.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Krok 1: przedstaw 8 obiektów. Krok 2: dołącz 3 kolejnych. Krok 3: policz lub rozłóż połączoną liczbę i otrzymaj 11. Krok 4: sprawdź, odejmując 3 od 11; otrzymujemy 8. Krok 1: przedstaw 9 obiektów. Krok 2: dołącz 5 kolejnych. Krok 3: policz lub rozłóż połączoną liczbę i otrzymaj 14. Krok 4: sprawdź, odejmując 5 od 14; otrzymujemy 9.
translations.commonMistakes: Cel tej lekcji: Dodawanie i odejmowanie — Add and Subtract Within 10. Nie traktuj znaku równości jak polecenia „napisz wynik”. Nie zmieniaj relacji w zadaniu tekstowym tylko dlatego, że inne działanie jest łatwiejsze. Sprawdź, czy wybrane działanie i wynik pasują do sytuacji.
translations.quickSummary: Cel tej lekcji: Dodawanie i odejmowanie — Add and Subtract Within 10. Przedstaw ilości, wybierz właściwą zależność dodawania lub odejmowania, wykonaj obliczenia dobrą strategią i sprawdź wynik w kontekście zadania.

translations.title: Add Within 50
translations.explanation: Add Within 50 is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Adding, Subtracting, and Working with Data”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.NBT.B.5. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction. Instructional focus: Students use the base-ten structure to read, compose, decompose, compare, round, and calculate with whole numbers or decimals at the grade-appropriate level. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Add Within 50. A digit has a value determined by its position. Moving one place left multiplies place value by 10; moving one place right divides it by 10. Reliable algorithms preserve place value by aligning like units and regrouping only when needed.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: The number 756 has 7 hundreds, 5 tens, and 6 ones, so 756 = 700 + 50 + 6. Adding 21 gives 756 + 21 = 777. Example 2: The number 782 has 7 hundreds, 8 tens, and 2 ones, so 782 = 700 + 80 + 2. Adding 23 gives 782 + 23 = 805.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: decompose 756 by place value. Step 2: decompose 21 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 777; estimate 756+about 21 to confirm the magnitude. Step 1: decompose 782 by place value. Step 2: decompose 23 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 805; estimate 782+about 23 to confirm the magnitude.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Add Within 50. Do not compare numbers by looking at only one digit. Keep place values aligned in written calculations, especially with decimals. Estimate before or after computing so that misplaced digits and unreasonable answers are detected.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Add Within 50. Use place value to represent the number, select an efficient operation or comparison strategy, and verify the magnitude of the result.

translations.title: Wartość pozycyjna i działania w systemie dziesiętnym — Add Within 50

Główny kierunek pracy: Uczeń wykorzystuje strukturę systemu dziesiętnego do odczytywania, składania, rozkładania, porównywania, zaokrąglania i wykonywania działań na liczbach całkowitych lub dziesiętnych odpowiednio do poziomu. Przesunięcie o jedno miejsce w lewo mnoży wartość pozycyjną przez 10, a w prawo dzieli ją przez 10. Poprawne algorytmy zachowują wartości pozycyjne przez ustawianie tych samych rzędów pod sobą i właściwe przegrupowanie.

translations.stepByStepSolutions: Krok 1: rozłóż 756 według wartości pozycyjnych. Krok 2: w razie potrzeby rozłóż 21. Krok 3: połącz te same rzędy i przegrupuj dziesięć jednostek w jednostkę wyższego rzędu. Krok 4: wynik to 777; oszacuj, aby sprawdzić jego wielkość. Krok 1: rozłóż 782 według wartości pozycyjnych. Krok 2: w razie potrzeby rozłóż 23. Krok 3: połącz te same rzędy i przegrupuj dziesięć jednostek w jednostkę wyższego rzędu. Krok 4: wynik to 805; oszacuj, aby sprawdzić jego wielkość.
translations.commonMistakes: Cel tej lekcji: Wartość pozycyjna i działania w systemie dziesiętnym — Add Within 50. Nie porównuj liczb na podstawie jednej cyfry. W zapisie działań ustawiaj te same wartości pozycyjne pod sobą, szczególnie przy liczbach dziesiętnych. Szacuj wynik, aby wykrywać przesunięte cyfry i nierozsądne odpowiedzi.
translations.quickSummary: Cel tej lekcji: Wartość pozycyjna i działania w systemie dziesiętnym — Add Within 50. Wykorzystaj wartość pozycyjną do przedstawienia liczby, wybierz skuteczną strategię działania lub porównania i sprawdź wielkość wyniku.

translations.title: Center Day 1 (optional)
translations.explanation: Center Day 1 (optional) is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Adding, Subtracting, and Working with Data”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.NBT.B.5, CCSS:2.OA.B.2. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction. Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies.2 By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers. Instructional focus: Students use the base-ten structure to read, compose, decompose, compare, round, and calculate with whole numbers or decimals at the grade-appropriate level. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Center Day 1 (optional). A digit has a value determined by its position. Moving one place left multiplies place value by 10; moving one place right divides it by 10. Reliable algorithms preserve place value by aligning like units and regrouping only when needed.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: The number 823 has 8 hundreds, 2 tens, and 3 ones, so 823 = 800 + 20 + 3. Adding 44 gives 823 + 44 = 867. Example 2: The number 757 has 7 hundreds, 5 tens, and 7 ones, so 757 = 700 + 50 + 7. Adding 13 gives 757 + 13 = 770.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: decompose 823 by place value. Step 2: decompose 44 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 867; estimate 823+about 44 to confirm the magnitude. Step 1: decompose 757 by place value. Step 2: decompose 13 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 770; estimate 757+about 13 to confirm the magnitude.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Center Day 1 (optional). Do not compare numbers by looking at only one digit. Keep place values aligned in written calculations, especially with decimals. Estimate before or after computing so that misplaced digits and unreasonable answers are detected.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Center Day 1 (optional). Use place value to represent the number, select an efficient operation or comparison strategy, and verify the magnitude of the result.

translations.title: Wartość pozycyjna i działania w systemie dziesiętnym — Center Day 1 (optional)
translations.explanation: Lekcja „Wartość pozycyjna i działania w systemie dziesiętnym — Center Day 1 (optional)” należy do działu „Adding, Subtracting, and Working with Data” i jest dokładnie powiązana ze standardami CCSS:2.NBT.B.5, CCSS:2.OA.B.2. Główny kierunek pracy: Uczeń wykorzystuje strukturę systemu dziesiętnego do odczytywania, składania, rozkładania, porównywania, zaokrąglania i wykonywania działań na liczbach całkowitych lub dziesiętnych odpowiednio do poziomu. Tytuł i kolejność pochodzą z zaakceptowanego źródła pedagogicznego, natomiast granice merytoryczne wyznaczają oficjalne standardy Common Core.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Cel tej lekcji: Wartość pozycyjna i działania w systemie dziesiętnym — Center Day 1 (optional). Wartość cyfry zależy od jej pozycji. Przesunięcie o jedno miejsce w lewo mnoży wartość pozycyjną przez 10, a w prawo dzieli ją przez 10. Poprawne algorytmy zachowują wartości pozycyjne przez ustawianie tych samych rzędów pod sobą i właściwe przegrupowanie.
translations.workedExamples: Przykład 1: Liczba 823 ma 8 setek, 2 dziesiątek i 3 jedności, więc 823 = 800 + 20 + 3. Po dodaniu 44 otrzymujemy 823 + 44 = 867. Przykład 2: Liczba 757 ma 7 setek, 5 dziesiątek i 7 jedności, więc 757 = 700 + 50 + 7. Po dodaniu 13 otrzymujemy 757 + 13 = 770.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Krok 1: rozłóż 823 według wartości pozycyjnych. Krok 2: w razie potrzeby rozłóż 44. Krok 3: połącz te same rzędy i przegrupuj dziesięć jednostek w jednostkę wyższego rzędu. Krok 4: wynik to 867; oszacuj, aby sprawdzić jego wielkość. Krok 1: rozłóż 757 według wartości pozycyjnych. Krok 2: w razie potrzeby rozłóż 13. Krok 3: połącz te same rzędy i przegrupuj dziesięć jednostek w jednostkę wyższego rzędu. Krok 4: wynik to 770; oszacuj, aby sprawdzić jego wielkość.
translations.commonMistakes: Cel tej lekcji: Wartość pozycyjna i działania w systemie dziesiętnym — Center Day 1 (optional). Nie porównuj liczb na podstawie jednej cyfry. translations.title: Interpret Picture Graphs
translations.explanation: Interpret Picture Graphs is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Adding, Subtracting, and Working with Data”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.MD.D.10. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put-together, take-apart, and compare problems4 using information presented in a bar graph. Instructional focus: Students connect measurable attributes with units, measurement procedures, representations of data, and calculations that answer a concrete question. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Interpret Picture Graphs. Choose a unit that matches the attribute, use equal-size units without gaps or overlaps, record the unit with the number, and interpret tables, line plots, clocks, money, area, volume, or angle measures according to the problem.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: A rectangle measures 11 units by 8 units. Its area is 11 × 8 = 88 square units, while its perimeter is 2(11+8) = 38 units. Example 2: A rectangle measures 7 units by 9 units. Its area is 7 × 9 = 63 square units, while its perimeter is 2(7+9) = 32 units.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: identify the requested attribute and units. Step 2: for area, multiply length by width: 11×8=88. Step 3: for perimeter, add all side lengths: 2(11+8)=38. Step 4: attach square units to area and linear units to perimeter. Step 1: identify the requested attribute and units. Step 2: for area, multiply length by width: 7×9=63. Step 3: for perimeter, add all side lengths: 2(7+9)=32. Step 4: attach square units to area and linear units to perimeter.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Interpret Picture Graphs. A number without its unit can be incomplete. Do not mix incompatible units before converting them. In graphs, read the scale and labels before drawing conclusions; in geometric measurement, distinguish length, area, angle, and volume.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Interpret Picture Graphs. Identify what is measured, choose or convert units correctly, calculate or read the representation, and state the result with its unit and meaning.

translations.title: Interpret Picture Wykresy
translations.explanation: Lekcja „Interpret Picture Wykresy” należy do działu „Adding, Subtracting, and Working with Data” i jest dokładnie powiązana ze standardami CCSS:2.MD.D.10. Główny kierunek pracy: Uczeń łączy mierzalne cechy z jednostkami, sposobem wykonywania pomiaru, reprezentacją danych i obliczeniami odpowiadającymi na konkretne pytanie. Tytuł i kolejność pochodzą z zaakceptowanego źródła pedagogicznego, natomiast granice merytoryczne wyznaczają oficjalne standardy Common Core.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Cel tej lekcji: Interpret Picture Wykresy. Dobierz jednostkę do mierzonej cechy, używaj jednostek jednakowej wielkości bez luk i nakładania, zapisuj jednostkę przy wyniku i interpretuj tabele, wykresy, czas, pieniądze, pole, objętość lub kąty zgodnie z zadaniem.
translations.workedExamples: Przykład 1: Prostokąt ma wymiary 11 na 8 jednostek. Pole wynosi 11 × 8 = 88 jednostek kwadratowych, a obwód 2(11+8) = 38 jednostek. Przykład 2: Prostokąt ma wymiary 7 na 9 jednostek. Pole wynosi 7 × 9 = 63 jednostek kwadratowych, a obwód 2(7+9) = 32 jednostek.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Krok 1: rozpoznaj mierzoną wielkość i jednostkę. Krok 2: pole: 11×8=88. Krok 3: obwód: 2(11+8)=38. Krok 4: przy polu zapisz jednostki kwadratowe, a przy obwodzie liniowe. Krok 1: rozpoznaj mierzoną wielkość i jednostkę. Krok 2: pole: 7×9=63. Krok 3: obwód: 2(7+9)=32. Krok 4: przy polu zapisz jednostki kwadratowe, a przy obwodzie liniowe.
translations.commonMistakes: Cel tej lekcji: Interpret Picture Wykresy. Liczba bez jednostki może być niepełną odpowiedzią. Nie łącz różnych jednostek bez przeliczenia. Na wykresie najpierw sprawdź skalę i opisy; w geometrii odróżniaj długość, pole, miarę kąta i objętość.
translations.quickSummary: Cel tej lekcji: Interpret Picture Wykresy. Ustal, co jest mierzone, prawidłowo dobierz lub przelicz jednostki, wykonaj obliczenie albo odczyt i podaj wynik z jednostką oraz znaczeniem.

translations.title: Diagrams with All Kinds of Compare Problems
translations.explanation: Diagrams with All Kinds of Compare Problems is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Adding, Subtracting, and Working with Data”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.OA.A.1, CCSS:2.OA.B.2. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.1 Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies.2 By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers. Instructional focus: Students connect quantities, counting strategies, equations, and story situations so that addition and subtraction represent meaningful relationships rather than isolated facts. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Diagrams with All Kinds of Compare Problems. Addition combines or increases quantities; subtraction separates, compares, or finds an unknown part. Equal sign means both expressions have the same value. Counting on/back, making ten, decomposing numbers, and inverse-operation reasoning are valid strategies when they fit the quantities.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: Start with 15 counters and add 6 more. The total is 15 + 6 = 21. A related subtraction fact is 21 - 6 = 15. Example 2: Start with 13 counters and add 4 more. The total is 13 + 4 = 17. A related subtraction fact is 17 - 4 = 13.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: represent 15 objects. Step 2: join 6 additional objects. Step 3: count or decompose the combined quantity to obtain 21. Step 4: check the relationship by subtracting 6 from 21; the result is 15. Step 1: represent 13 objects. Step 2: join 4 additional objects. Step 3: count or decompose the combined quantity to obtain 17. Step 4: check the relationship by subtracting 4 from 17; the result is 13.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Diagrams with All Kinds of Compare Problems. Do not treat the equal sign as an instruction to write the next answer. Do not change a story relationship merely to make the arithmetic easier. Check whether the chosen operation and the final number are reasonable for the situation.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Diagrams with All Kinds of Compare Problems. Represent the quantities, choose an addition or subtraction relationship, calculate with a suitable strategy, and check the result against the original situation.

translations.title: Diagrams with All Kinds of Porównywanie Problems

translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Cel tej lekcji: Diagrams with All Kinds of Porównywanie Problems. Dodawanie łączy lub zwiększa ilości; odejmowanie rozdziela, porównuje albo wyznacza brakującą część. Znak równości oznacza tę samą wartość po obu stronach. Liczenie w przód i wstecz, dopełnianie do dziesięciu, rozkład liczb oraz działania odwrotne są poprawnymi strategiami.
translations.workedExamples: Przykład 1: Mamy 15 liczników i dokładamy 6. Razem jest 15 + 6 = 21. Powiązany fakt odejmowania to 21 - 6 = 15. Przykład 2: Mamy 13 liczników i dokładamy 4. Razem jest 13 + 4 = 17. Powiązany fakt odejmowania to 17 - 4 = 13.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Krok 1: przedstaw 15 obiektów. Krok 2: dołącz 6 kolejnych. Krok 3: policz lub rozłóż połączoną liczbę i otrzymaj 21. Krok 4: sprawdź, odejmując 6 od 21; otrzymujemy 15. Krok 1: przedstaw 13 obiektów. Krok 2: dołącz 4 kolejnych. Krok 3: policz lub rozłóż połączoną liczbę i otrzymaj 17. Krok 4: sprawdź, odejmując 4 od 17; otrzymujemy 13.
translations.commonMistakes: Cel tej lekcji: Diagrams with All Kinds of Porównywanie Problems. Nie traktuj znaku równości jak polecenia „napisz wynik”. Nie zmieniaj relacji w zadaniu tekstowym tylko dlatego, że inne działanie jest łatwiejsze. Sprawdź, czy wybrane działanie i wynik pasują do sytuacji.
translations.quickSummary: Cel tej lekcji: Diagrams with All Kinds of Porównywanie Problems. Przedstaw ilości, wybierz właściwą zależność dodawania lub odejmowania, wykonaj obliczenia dobrą strategią i sprawdź wynik w kontekście zadania.

translations.title: Center Day 3 (optional)
translations.explanation: Center Day 3 (optional) is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Adding, Subtracting, and Working with Data”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.MD.D.10, CCSS:2.NBT.A.2, CCSS:2.NBT.B.5. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put-together, take-apart, and compare problems4 using information presented in a bar graph. Count within 1000; skip-count by 5s, 10s, and 100s. Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction. Instructional focus: Students use the base-ten structure to read, compose, decompose, compare, round, and calculate with whole numbers or decimals at the grade-appropriate level. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Center Day 3 (optional). A digit has a value determined by its position. Moving one place left multiplies place value by 10; moving one place right divides it by 10. Reliable algorithms preserve place value by aligning like units and regrouping only when needed.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: The number 412 has 4 hundreds, 1 tens, and 2 ones, so 412 = 400 + 10 + 2. Adding 19 gives 412 + 19 = 431. Example 2: The number 656 has 6 hundreds, 5 tens, and 6 ones, so 656 = 600 + 50 + 6. Adding 61 gives 656 + 61 = 717.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: decompose 412 by place value. Step 2: decompose 19 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 431; estimate 412+about 19 to confirm the magnitude. Step 1: decompose 656 by place value. Step 2: decompose 61 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 717; estimate 656+about 61 to confirm the magnitude.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Center Day 3 (optional). Do not compare numbers by looking at only one digit. Keep place values aligned in written calculations, especially with decimals. Estimate before or after computing so that misplaced digits and unreasonable answers are detected.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Center Day 3 (optional). Use place value to represent the number, select an efficient operation or comparison strategy, and verify the magnitude of the result.

translations.title: Measure in Centimeters PLC Activity
translations.explanation: Measure in Centimeters PLC Activity is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Measuring Length”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.MD.A.1, CCSS:2.MD.A.4. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes. Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit. Instructional focus: Students connect measurable attributes with units, measurement procedures, representations of data, and calculations that answer a concrete question. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Measure in Centimeters PLC Activity. Choose a unit that matches the attribute, use equal-size units without gaps or overlaps, record the unit with the number, and interpret tables, line plots, clocks, money, area, volume, or angle measures according to the problem.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: A rectangle measures 3 units by 2 units. Its area is 3 × 2 = 6 square units, while its perimeter is 2(3+2) = 10 units. Example 2: A rectangle measures 10 units by 3 units. Its area is 10 × 3 = 30 square units, while its perimeter is 2(10+3) = 26 units.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: identify the requested attribute and units. Step 2: for area, multiply length by width: 3×2=6. Step 3: for perimeter, add all side lengths: 2(3+2)=10. Step 4: attach square units to area and linear units to perimeter. Step 1: identify the requested attribute and units. Step 2: for area, multiply length by width: 10×3=30. Step 3: for perimeter, add all side lengths: 2(10+3)=26. Step 4: attach square units to area and linear units to perimeter.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Measure in Centimeters PLC Activity. A number without its unit can be incomplete. Do not mix incompatible units before converting them. In graphs, read the scale and labels before drawing conclusions; in geometric measurement, distinguish length, area, angle, and volume.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Measure in Centimeters PLC Activity. Identify what is measured, choose or convert units correctly, calculate or read the representation, and state the result with its unit and meaning.

translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Compare Reptile Lengths in Story Problems. Addition combines or increases quantities; subtraction separates, compares, or finds an unknown part. Equal sign means both expressions have the same value. Counting on/back, making ten, decomposing numbers, and inverse-operation reasoning are valid strategies when they fit the quantities.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: Start with 16 counters and add 2 more. The total is 16 + 2 = 18. A related subtraction fact is 18 - 2 = 16. Example 2: Start with 13 counters and add 6 more. The total is 13 + 6 = 19. A related subtraction fact is 19 - 6 = 13.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: represent 16 objects. Step 2: join 2 additional objects. Step 3: count or decompose the combined quantity to obtain 18. Step 3: count or decompose the combined quantity to obtain 19. Step 4: check the relationship by subtracting 6 from 19; the result is 13.

translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Compare Reptile Lengths in Story Problems. Represent the quantities, choose an addition or subtraction relationship, calculate with a suitable strategy, and check the result against the original situation.

translations.title: Measure with a Torn Tape
translations.explanation: Measure with a Torn Tape is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Measuring Length”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.OA.B.2. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies.2 By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Measure with a Torn Tape. Addition combines or increases quantities; subtraction separates, compares, or finds an unknown part. Equal sign means both expressions have the same value. Counting on/back, making ten, decomposing numbers, and inverse-operation reasoning are valid strategies when they fit the quantities.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: Start with 8 counters and add 2 more. The total is 8 + 2 = 10. A related subtraction fact is 10 - 2 = 8. Example 2: Start with 11 counters and add 4 more. The total is 11 + 4 = 15. A related subtraction fact is 15 - 4 = 11.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: represent 8 objects. Step 2: join 2 additional objects. Step 3: count or decompose the combined quantity to obtain 10. Step 4: check the relationship by subtracting 2 from 10; the result is 8. Step 1: represent 11 objects. Step 2: join 4 additional objects. Step 3: count or decompose the combined quantity to obtain 15. Step 4: check the relationship by subtracting 4 from 15; the result is 11.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Measure with a Torn Tape. Do not treat the equal sign as an instruction to write the next answer. Do not change a story relationship merely to make the arithmetic easier. Check whether the chosen operation and the final number are reasonable for the situation.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Measure with a Torn Tape. Represent the quantities, choose an addition or subtraction relationship, calculate with a suitable strategy, and check the result against the original situation.

translations.title: How Do We Compose a Hundred?
translations.explanation: How Do We Compose a Hundred? is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Numbers to 1,000”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.NBT.A.1, CCSS:2.NBT.A.2. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones. Understand the following as special cases: a. 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens — called a “hundred.” b. The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones). Count within 1000; skip-count by 5s, 10s, and 100s. Instructional focus: Students use the base-ten structure to read, compose, decompose, compare, round, and calculate with whole numbers or decimals at the grade-appropriate level. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: How Do We Compose a Hundred?. A digit has a value determined by its position. Moving one place left multiplies place value by 10; moving one place right divides it by 10. Reliable algorithms preserve place value by aligning like units and regrouping only when needed.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: The number 638 has 6 hundreds, 3 tens, and 8 ones, so 638 = 600 + 30 + 8. Adding 62 gives 638 + 62 = 700. Example 2: The number 757 has 7 hundreds, 5 tens, and 7 ones, so 757 = 700 + 50 + 7. Adding 46 gives 757 + 46 = 803.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: decompose 638 by place value. Step 2: decompose 62 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 700; estimate 638+about 62 to confirm the magnitude. Step 1: decompose 757 by place value. Step 2: decompose 46 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 803; estimate 757+about 46 to confirm the magnitude.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: How Do We Compose a Hundred?. Do not compare numbers by looking at only one digit. Keep place values aligned in written calculations, especially with decimals. Estimate before or after computing so that misplaced digits and unreasonable answers are detected.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: How Do We Compose a Hundred?. Use place value to represent the number, select an efficient operation or comparison strategy, and verify the magnitude of the result.

translations.title: Order Numbers
translations.explanation: Order Numbers is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Numbers to 1,000”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.NBT.A.1, CCSS:2.NBT.A.4, CCSS:2.NBT.B.8. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones. The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones). translations.title: Identify and Sort Shapes
translations.explanation: Identify and Sort Shapes is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Geometry, Time, and Money”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.G.A.1. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Recognize and draw shapes having specified attributes, such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces.5 Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes. Instructional focus: Students describe, compose, decompose, compare, and reason about shapes using defining properties rather than appearance alone. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Identify and Sort Shapes. Geometric claims should use properties such as sides, angles, parallel or perpendicular lines, symmetry, coordinates, congruence, similarity, or equal partitions as appropriate. A drawing is evidence only when its marked or known properties justify the conclusion.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: A rectangle with side lengths 6 and 4 has four right angles and opposite sides of equal length. Its area is 6 × 4 = 24 square units. Example 2: A rectangle with side lengths 5 and 2 has four right angles and opposite sides of equal length. Its area is 5 × 2 = 10 square units.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: identify defining properties: four sides and four right angles. Step 2: use the given side lengths 6 and 4. Step 3: multiply to obtain area 24. Step 4: note that rotating the rectangle would not change its defining properties. Step 1: identify defining properties: four sides and four right angles. Step 2: use the given side lengths 5 and 2. Step 3: multiply to obtain area 10. Step 4: note that rotating the rectangle would not change its defining properties.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Identify and Sort Shapes. Do not classify a shape by orientation, color, or size when those are not defining attributes. Do not assume an angle or length from appearance; use the stated properties or calculate them.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Identify and Sort Shapes. Name the relevant properties, represent the figure accurately, reason from those properties, and verify that the conclusion remains true when the picture changes orientation or scale.

Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Center Day 1 (optional). A digit has a value determined by its position. Moving one place left multiplies place value by 10; moving one place right divides it by 10. Reliable algorithms preserve place value by aligning like units and regrouping only when needed.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: The number 665 has 6 hundreds, 6 tens, and 5 ones, so 665 = 600 + 60 + 5. Adding 66 gives 665 + 66 = 731. Example 2: The number 765 has 7 hundreds, 6 tens, and 5 ones, so 765 = 700 + 60 + 5. Adding 13 gives 765 + 13 = 778.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: decompose 665 by place value. Step 2: decompose 66 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 731; estimate 665+about 66 to confirm the magnitude. Step 1: decompose 765 by place value. Step 2: decompose 13 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 778; estimate 765+about 13 to confirm the magnitude.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Center Day 1 (optional). Do not compare numbers by looking at only one digit. translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Center Day 1 (optional). Use place value to represent the number, select an efficient operation or comparison strategy, and verify the magnitude of the result.

Tytuł i kolejność pochodzą z zaakceptowanego źródła pedagogicznego, natomiast granice merytoryczne wyznaczają oficjalne standardy Common Core.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Cel tej lekcji: Wartość pozycyjna i działania w systemie dziesiętnym — Decompose a Ten and a Hundred to Subtract. Wartość cyfry zależy od jej pozycji. Przesunięcie o jedno miejsce w lewo mnoży wartość pozycyjną przez 10, a w prawo dzieli ją przez 10. Poprawne algorytmy zachowują wartości pozycyjne przez ustawianie tych samych rzędów pod sobą i właściwe przegrupowanie.
translations.workedExamples: Przykład 1: Liczba 656 ma 6 setek, 5 dziesiątek i 6 jedności, więc 656 = 600 + 50 + 6. Po dodaniu 48 otrzymujemy 656 + 48 = 704. Przykład 2: Liczba 398 ma 3 setek, 9 dziesiątek i 8 jedności, więc 398 = 300 + 90 + 8. Po dodaniu 33 otrzymujemy 398 + 33 = 431.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Krok 1: rozłóż 656 według wartości pozycyjnych. Krok 2: w razie potrzeby rozłóż 48. Krok 3: połącz te same rzędy i przegrupuj dziesięć jednostek w jednostkę wyższego rzędu. Krok 4: wynik to 704; oszacuj, aby sprawdzić jego wielkość. Krok 1: rozłóż 398 według wartości pozycyjnych. translations.commonMistakes: Cel tej lekcji: Wartość pozycyjna i działania w systemie dziesiętnym — Decompose a Ten and a Hundred to Subtract. Nie porównuj liczb na podstawie jednej cyfry. translations.title: Subtract Within 1,000
translations.explanation: Subtract Within 1,000 is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Adding and Subtracting within 1,000”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.NBT.A.1, CCSS:2.NBT.B.7, CCSS:2.NBT.B.9. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones. Understand the following as special cases: a. 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens — called a “hundred.” b. The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones). Add and subtract within 1000, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. Understand that in adding or subtracting three-digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds. Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations.3 2See standard 1.OA.6 for a list of mental strategies. 3Explanations may be supported by drawings or objects. Instructional focus: Students use the base-ten structure to read, compose, decompose, compare, round, and calculate with whole numbers or decimals at the grade-appropriate level. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Subtract Within 1,000. A digit has a value determined by its position. Moving one place left multiplies place value by 10; moving one place right divides it by 10. Reliable algorithms preserve place value by aligning like units and regrouping only when needed.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: The number 814 has 8 hundreds, 1 tens, and 4 ones, so 814 = 800 + 10 + 4. Adding 22 gives 814 + 22 = 836. Example 2: The number 765 has 7 hundreds, 6 tens, and 5 ones, so 765 = 700 + 60 + 5. Adding 54 gives 765 + 54 = 819.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: decompose 814 by place value. Step 2: decompose 22 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 836; estimate 814+about 22 to confirm the magnitude. Step 1: decompose 765 by place value. Step 2: decompose 54 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 819; estimate 765+about 54 to confirm the magnitude.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Subtract Within 1,000. Do not compare numbers by looking at only one digit. Keep place values aligned in written calculations, especially with decimals. Estimate before or after computing so that misplaced digits and unreasonable answers are detected.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Subtract Within 1,000. Use place value to represent the number, select an efficient operation or comparison strategy, and verify the magnitude of the result.

translations.title: Partners Make Pairs
translations.explanation: Partners Make Pairs is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Equal Groups”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.OA.C.3. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members, e.g., by pairing objects or counting them by 2s; write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends. Instructional focus: Students connect quantities, counting strategies, equations, and story situations so that addition and subtraction represent meaningful relationships rather than isolated facts. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Partners Make Pairs. Addition combines or increases quantities; subtraction separates, compares, or finds an unknown part. Equal sign means both expressions have the same value. Counting on/back, making ten, decomposing numbers, and inverse-operation reasoning are valid strategies when they fit the quantities.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: Start with 8 counters and add 2 more. The total is 8 + 2 = 10. A related subtraction fact is 10 - 2 = 8. Example 2: Start with 15 counters and add 3 more. The total is 15 + 3 = 18. A related subtraction fact is 18 - 3 = 15.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: represent 8 objects. Step 2: join 2 additional objects. Step 3: count or decompose the combined quantity to obtain 10. Step 4: check the relationship by subtracting 2 from 10; the result is 8. Step 1: represent 15 objects. Step 2: join 3 additional objects. Step 3: count or decompose the combined quantity to obtain 18. Step 4: check the relationship by subtracting 3 from 18; the result is 15.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Partners Make Pairs. Do not treat the equal sign as an instruction to write the next answer. Do not change a story relationship merely to make the arithmetic easier. Check whether the chosen operation and the final number are reasonable for the situation.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Partners Make Pairs. Represent the quantities, choose an addition or subtraction relationship, calculate with a suitable strategy, and check the result against the original situation.

translations.title: Dodawanie i odejmowanie — Partners Make Pairs

Główny kierunek pracy: Uczeń łączy liczebność zbiorów, strategie liczenia, równania i sytuacje tekstowe, tak aby dodawanie i odejmowanie opisywały rzeczywiste zależności, a nie tylko pojedyncze fakty rachunkowe. Tytuł i kolejność pochodzą z zaakceptowanego źródła pedagogicznego, natomiast granice merytoryczne wyznaczają oficjalne standardy Common Core.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Cel tej lekcji: Dodawanie i odejmowanie — Partners Make Pairs. Dodawanie łączy lub zwiększa ilości; odejmowanie rozdziela, porównuje albo wyznacza brakującą część. Znak równości oznacza tę samą wartość po obu stronach. Liczenie w przód i wstecz, dopełnianie do dziesięciu, rozkład liczb oraz działania odwrotne są poprawnymi strategiami.
translations.workedExamples: Przykład 1: Mamy 8 liczników i dokładamy 2. Razem jest 8 + 2 = 10. Powiązany fakt odejmowania to 10 - 2 = 8. Przykład 2: Mamy 15 liczników i dokładamy 3. Razem jest 15 + 3 = 18. Powiązany fakt odejmowania to 18 - 3 = 15.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Krok 1: przedstaw 8 obiektów. Krok 2: dołącz 2 kolejnych. Krok 3: policz lub rozłóż połączoną liczbę i otrzymaj 10. Krok 4: sprawdź, odejmując 2 od 10; otrzymujemy 8. Krok 1: przedstaw 15 obiektów. Krok 2: dołącz 3 kolejnych. Krok 3: policz lub rozłóż połączoną liczbę i otrzymaj 18. Krok 4: sprawdź, odejmując 3 od 18; otrzymujemy 15.
translations.commonMistakes: Cel tej lekcji: Dodawanie i odejmowanie — Partners Make Pairs. Nie traktuj znaku równości jak polecenia „napisz wynik”. Nie zmieniaj relacji w zadaniu tekstowym tylko dlatego, że inne działanie jest łatwiejsze. Sprawdź, czy wybrane działanie i wynik pasują do sytuacji.
translations.quickSummary: Cel tej lekcji: Dodawanie i odejmowanie — Partners Make Pairs. Przedstaw ilości, wybierz właściwą zależność dodawania lub odejmowania, wykonaj obliczenia dobrą strategią i sprawdź wynik w kontekście zadania.

The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Count within 1000; skip-count by 5s, 10s, and 100s. Add and subtract within 1000, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. Understand that in adding or subtracting three-digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds. Mentally add 10 or 100 to a given number 100–900, and mentally subtract 10 or 100 from a given number 100–900. Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies.2 By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers. Instructional focus: Students use the base-ten structure to read, compose, decompose, compare, round, and calculate with whole numbers or decimals at the grade-appropriate level. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Center Day 1 (optional). A digit has a value determined by its position. Moving one place left multiplies place value by 10; moving one place right divides it by 10. Reliable algorithms preserve place value by aligning like units and regrouping only when needed.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: The number 877 has 8 hundreds, 7 tens, and 7 ones, so 877 = 800 + 70 + 7. Adding 24 gives 877 + 24 = 901. Example 2: The number 288 has 2 hundreds, 8 tens, and 8 ones, so 288 = 200 + 80 + 8. Adding 55 gives 288 + 55 = 343.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: decompose 877 by place value. Step 2: decompose 24 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 901; estimate 877+about 24 to confirm the magnitude. Step 1: decompose 288 by place value. Step 2: decompose 55 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 343; estimate 288+about 55 to confirm the magnitude.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Center Day 1 (optional). Do not compare numbers by looking at only one digit. Keep place values aligned in written calculations, especially with decimals. Estimate before or after computing so that misplaced digits and unreasonable answers are detected.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Center Day 1 (optional). Use place value to represent the number, select an efficient operation or comparison strategy, and verify the magnitude of the result.

translations.title: What is an Array?
translations.explanation: What is an Array? is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Equal Groups”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.OA.B.2, CCSS:2.OA.C.3, CCSS:2.OA.C.4. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies.2 By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers. Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members, e.g., by pairing objects or counting them by 2s; write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends. Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and up to 5 columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends. 1See Glossary, Table 1. Instructional focus: Students reason about equal groups, arrays, factors, products, quotients, and unknown group sizes. Multiplication and division are connected inverse relationships. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: What is an Array?. A product can represent equal groups or rows and columns. Division can ask how many groups or how many objects are in each group. Factor pairs describe the same product, and multiplication can be checked with division.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: Arrange 9 equal groups with 3 objects in each group. The product is 9 × 3 = 27; therefore 27 ÷ 9 = 3. Example 2: Arrange 7 equal groups with 6 objects in each group. The product is 7 × 6 = 42; therefore 42 ÷ 7 = 6.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: identify 9 groups and 3 objects per group. Step 2: multiply 9 by 3 to get 27. Step 3: interpret 27 as the total. Step 4: check with the inverse relationship 27 ÷ 9 = 3. Step 1: identify 7 groups and 6 objects per group. Step 2: multiply 7 by 6 to get 42. Step 3: interpret 42 as the total. Step 4: check with the inverse relationship 42 ÷ 7 = 6.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: What is an Array?. Do not swap the meaning of number of groups and size of each group without checking the context. A remainder must be interpreted, not ignored automatically. Verify division by multiplying the quotient by the divisor when appropriate.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: What is an Array?. Model equal groups clearly, connect multiplication with division, compute accurately, and interpret the answer in context.

Dzielenie może pytać o liczbę grup lub liczbę elementów w każdej grupie. Pary czynników dają ten sam iloczyn, a mnożenie można sprawdzić dzieleniem.
translations.workedExamples: Przykład 1: Ułóż 9 równych grup po 3 elementów. Iloczyn wynosi 9 × 3 = 27, więc 27 ÷ 9 = 3. Przykład 2: Ułóż 7 równych grup po 6 elementów. Iloczyn wynosi 7 × 6 = 42, więc 42 ÷ 7 = 6.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Krok 1: rozpoznaj 9 grup po 3 elementów. Krok 2: pomnóż 9 przez 3 i otrzymaj 27. Krok 3: zinterpretuj 27 jako całość. Krok 4: sprawdź działaniem odwrotnym 27 ÷ 9 = 3. Krok 1: rozpoznaj 7 grup po 6 elementów. Krok 2: pomnóż 7 przez 6 i otrzymaj 42. Krok 3: zinterpretuj 42 jako całość. Krok 4: sprawdź działaniem odwrotnym 42 ÷ 7 = 6.
translations.commonMistakes: Cel tej lekcji: Mnożenie i dzielenie — What is an Array?. Nie zamieniaj bez sprawdzenia liczby grup z liczbą elementów w grupie. Resztę z dzielenia trzeba zinterpretować, a nie automatycznie pominąć. Gdy to możliwe, sprawdzaj dzielenie za pomocą mnożenia.
translations.quickSummary: Cel tej lekcji: Mnożenie i dzielenie — What is an Array?. Wyraźnie modeluj równe grupy, łącz mnożenie z dzieleniem, licz dokładnie i interpretuj wynik w kontekście.

translations.title: Write Expressions and Equations to Represent Arrays
translations.explanation: Write Expressions and Equations to Represent Arrays is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Equal Groups”. Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and up to 5 columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends. 1See Glossary, Table 1. Instructional focus: Students reason about equal groups, arrays, factors, products, quotients, and unknown group sizes. Multiplication and division are connected inverse relationships. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Write Expressions and Equations to Represent Arrays. A product can represent equal groups or rows and columns. Division can ask how many groups or how many objects are in each group. Factor pairs describe the same product, and multiplication can be checked with division.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: Arrange 5 equal groups with 2 objects in each group. The product is 5 × 2 = 10; therefore 10 ÷ 5 = 2. Example 2: Arrange 6 equal groups with 5 objects in each group. The product is 6 × 5 = 30; therefore 30 ÷ 6 = 5.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: identify 5 groups and 2 objects per group. Step 2: multiply 5 by 2 to get 10. Step 3: interpret 10 as the total. Step 4: check with the inverse relationship 10 ÷ 5 = 2. Step 1: identify 6 groups and 5 objects per group. Step 2: multiply 6 by 5 to get 30. Step 3: interpret 30 as the total. Step 4: check with the inverse relationship 30 ÷ 6 = 5.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Write Expressions and Equations to Represent Arrays. Do not swap the meaning of number of groups and size of each group without checking the context. A remainder must be interpreted, not ignored automatically. Verify division by multiplying the quotient by the divisor when appropriate.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Write Expressions and Equations to Represent Arrays. Model equal groups clearly, connect multiplication with division, compute accurately, and interpret the answer in context.

translations.workedExamples: Example 1: A rectangle with side lengths 6 and 5 has four right angles and opposite sides of equal length. Its area is 6 × 5 = 30 square units. Example 2: A rectangle with side lengths 9 and 6 has four right angles and opposite sides of equal length. Its area is 9 × 6 = 54 square units.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: identify defining properties: four sides and four right angles. Step 2: use the given side lengths 6 and 5. Step 3: multiply to obtain area 30. Step 4: note that rotating the rectangle would not change its defining properties. Step 1: identify defining properties: four sides and four right angles. Step 2: use the given side lengths 9 and 6. translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Partition Rectangles into Squares. Do not classify a shape by orientation, color, or size when those are not defining attributes. Do not assume an angle or length from appearance; use the stated properties or calculate them.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Partition Rectangles into Squares. Name the relevant properties, represent the figure accurately, reason from those properties, and verify that the conclusion remains true when the picture changes orientation or scale.

translations.title: Center Day 2 (optional)
translations.explanation: Center Day 2 (optional) is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Equal Groups”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.NBT.A.2, CCSS:2.NBT.B.7. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Count within 1000; skip-count by 5s, 10s, and 100s. Add and subtract within 1000, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. Understand that in adding or subtracting three-digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds. Instructional focus: Students use the base-ten structure to read, compose, decompose, compare, round, and calculate with whole numbers or decimals at the grade-appropriate level. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Center Day 2 (optional). A digit has a value determined by its position. Moving one place left multiplies place value by 10; moving one place right divides it by 10. Reliable algorithms preserve place value by aligning like units and regrouping only when needed.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: The number 493 has 4 hundreds, 9 tens, and 3 ones, so 493 = 400 + 90 + 3. Adding 34 gives 493 + 34 = 527. Example 2: The number 425 has 4 hundreds, 2 tens, and 5 ones, so 425 = 400 + 20 + 5. Adding 33 gives 425 + 33 = 458.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: decompose 493 by place value. Step 2: decompose 34 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 527; estimate 493+about 34 to confirm the magnitude. Step 1: decompose 425 by place value. Step 2: decompose 33 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 458; estimate 425+about 33 to confirm the magnitude.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Center Day 2 (optional). Do not compare numbers by looking at only one digit. Keep place values aligned in written calculations, especially with decimals. Estimate before or after computing so that misplaced digits and unreasonable answers are detected.

translations.title: Measure on a Map PLC Activity
translations.explanation: Measure on a Map PLC Activity is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Putting It All Together”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.MD.A.1, CCSS:2.MD.A.4, CCSS:2.MD.B.5, CCSS:2.OA.B.2. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes. Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit. Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as drawings of rulers) and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem. Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies.2 By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers. Instructional focus: Students connect measurable attributes with units, measurement procedures, representations of data, and calculations that answer a concrete question. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Measure on a Map PLC Activity. Choose a unit that matches the attribute, use equal-size units without gaps or overlaps, record the unit with the number, and interpret tables, line plots, clocks, money, area, volume, or angle measures according to the problem.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: A rectangle measures 8 units by 4 units. Its area is 8 × 4 = 32 square units, while its perimeter is 2(8+4) = 24 units. Example 2: A rectangle measures 6 units by 5 units. Its area is 6 × 5 = 30 square units, while its perimeter is 2(6+5) = 22 units.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: identify the requested attribute and units. Step 2: for area, multiply length by width: 8×4=32. Step 3: for perimeter, add all side lengths: 2(8+4)=24. Step 4: attach square units to area and linear units to perimeter. Step 1: identify the requested attribute and units. Step 2: for area, multiply length by width: 6×5=30. Step 3: for perimeter, add all side lengths: 2(6+5)=22. Step 4: attach square units to area and linear units to perimeter.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Measure on a Map PLC Activity. A number without its unit can be incomplete. Do not mix incompatible units before converting them. In graphs, read the scale and labels before drawing conclusions; in geometric measurement, distinguish length, area, angle, and volume.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Measure on a Map PLC Activity. Identify what is measured, choose or convert units correctly, calculate or read the representation, and state the result with its unit and meaning.

translations.title: Compose and Decompose Numbers Within 1,000 PLC Activity
translations.explanation: Compose and Decompose Numbers Within 1,000 PLC Activity is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Putting It All Together”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.NBT.A.1. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones. Understand the following as special cases: a. 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens — called a “hundred.” b. The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones). Instructional focus: Students use the base-ten structure to read, compose, decompose, compare, round, and calculate with whole numbers or decimals at the grade-appropriate level. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: Compose and Decompose Numbers Within 1,000 PLC Activity. A digit has a value determined by its position. Moving one place left multiplies place value by 10; moving one place right divides it by 10. Reliable algorithms preserve place value by aligning like units and regrouping only when needed.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: The number 586 has 5 hundreds, 8 tens, and 6 ones, so 586 = 500 + 80 + 6. Adding 14 gives 586 + 14 = 600. Example 2: The number 891 has 8 hundreds, 9 tens, and 1 ones, so 891 = 800 + 90 + 1. Adding 15 gives 891 + 15 = 906.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: decompose 586 by place value. Step 2: decompose 14 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 600; estimate 586+about 14 to confirm the magnitude. Step 1: decompose 891 by place value. Step 2: decompose 15 if helpful. Step 3: combine like place-value units and regroup when ten of a unit are formed. Step 4: the sum is 906; estimate 891+about 15 to confirm the magnitude.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: Compose and Decompose Numbers Within 1,000 PLC Activity. Do not compare numbers by looking at only one digit. Keep place values aligned in written calculations, especially with decimals. Estimate before or after computing so that misplaced digits and unreasonable answers are detected.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: Compose and Decompose Numbers Within 1,000 PLC Activity. Use place value to represent the number, select an efficient operation or comparison strategy, and verify the magnitude of the result.

translations.title: Represent Numbers with Expressions
translations.explanation: Represent Numbers with Expressions is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Putting It All Together”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.NBT.A.1, CCSS:2.NBT.A.3. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones. Understand the following as special cases: a. 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens — called a “hundred.” b. The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones). translations.workedExamples: Example 1: The number 286 has 2 hundreds, 8 tens, and 6 ones, so 286 = 200 + 80 + 6. Adding 54 gives 286 + 54 = 340. Example 2: The number 277 has 2 hundreds, 7 tens, and 7 ones, so 277 = 200 + 70 + 7. Adding 37 gives 277 + 37 = 314.

translations.title: What’s the Story?
translations.explanation: What’s the Story? is an Edulytics lesson in the unit “Putting It All Together”. It is aligned exactly to CCSS:2.OA.A.1. The accepted Common Core target text for this lesson states: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.1 Instructional focus: Students connect quantities, counting strategies, equations, and story situations so that addition and subtraction represent meaningful relationships rather than isolated facts. The lesson title and source sequence determine the immediate context, while the official Standard text controls the academic boundary.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Lesson-specific focus: What’s the Story?. Addition combines or increases quantities; subtraction separates, compares, or finds an unknown part. Equal sign means both expressions have the same value. Counting on/back, making ten, decomposing numbers, and inverse-operation reasoning are valid strategies when they fit the quantities.
translations.workedExamples: Example 1: Start with 9 counters and add 4 more. The total is 9 + 4 = 13. A related subtraction fact is 13 - 4 = 9. Example 2: Start with 16 counters and add 3 more. The total is 16 + 3 = 19. A related subtraction fact is 19 - 3 = 16.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Step 1: represent 9 objects. Step 2: join 4 additional objects. Step 3: count or decompose the combined quantity to obtain 13. Step 4: check the relationship by subtracting 4 from 13; the result is 9. Step 1: represent 16 objects. Step 2: join 3 additional objects. Step 3: count or decompose the combined quantity to obtain 19. Step 4: check the relationship by subtracting 3 from 19; the result is 16.
translations.commonMistakes: Lesson-specific focus: What’s the Story?. Do not treat the equal sign as an instruction to write the next answer. Do not change a story relationship merely to make the arithmetic easier. Check whether the chosen operation and the final number are reasonable for the situation.
translations.quickSummary: Lesson-specific focus: What’s the Story?. Represent the quantities, choose an addition or subtraction relationship, calculate with a suitable strategy, and check the result against the original situation.

translations.title: Dodawanie i odejmowanie — What’s the Story?
translations.explanation: Lekcja „Dodawanie i odejmowanie — What’s the Story?” należy do działu „Putting It All Together” i jest dokładnie powiązana ze standardami CCSS:2.OA.A.1. Główny kierunek pracy: Uczeń łączy liczebność zbiorów, strategie liczenia, równania i sytuacje tekstowe, tak aby dodawanie i odejmowanie opisywały rzeczywiste zależności, a nie tylko pojedyncze fakty rachunkowe. Tytuł i kolejność pochodzą z zaakceptowanego źródła pedagogicznego, natomiast granice merytoryczne wyznaczają oficjalne standardy Common Core.
translations.keyConceptsAndRules: Cel tej lekcji: Dodawanie i odejmowanie — What’s the Story?. Dodawanie łączy lub zwiększa ilości; odejmowanie rozdziela, porównuje albo wyznacza brakującą część. Znak równości oznacza tę samą wartość po obu stronach. Liczenie w przód i wstecz, dopełnianie do dziesięciu, rozkład liczb oraz działania odwrotne są poprawnymi strategiami.
translations.workedExamples: Przykład 1: Mamy 9 liczników i dokładamy 4. Razem jest 9 + 4 = 13. Powiązany fakt odejmowania to 13 - 4 = 9. Przykład 2: Mamy 16 liczników i dokładamy 3. Razem jest 16 + 3 = 19. Powiązany fakt odejmowania to 19 - 3 = 16.
translations.stepByStepSolutions: Krok 1: przedstaw 9 obiektów. Krok 2: dołącz 4 kolejnych. Krok 3: policz lub rozłóż połączoną liczbę i otrzymaj 13. Krok 4: sprawdź, odejmując 4 od 13; otrzymujemy 9. Krok 1: przedstaw 16 obiektów. Krok 2: dołącz 3 kolejnych. Krok 3: policz lub rozłóż połączoną liczbę i otrzymaj 19. Krok 4: sprawdź, odejmując 3 od 19; otrzymujemy 16.
translations.commonMistakes: Cel tej lekcji: Dodawanie i odejmowanie — What’s the Story?. Nie traktuj znaku równości jak polecenia „napisz wynik”. Nie zmieniaj relacji w zadaniu tekstowym tylko dlatego, że inne działanie jest łatwiejsze. Sprawdź, czy wybrane działanie i wynik pasują do sytuacji.
translations.quickSummary: Cel tej lekcji: Dodawanie i odejmowanie — What’s the Story?. Przedstaw ilości, wybierz właściwą zależność dodawania lub odejmowania, wykonaj obliczenia dobrą strategią i sprawdź wynik w kontekście zadania.
